correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and rate limits are explicit. The two-state formula has manifestly nonnegative component coefficients; trace and Cayley–Hamilton prove full stochasticity and the identity M_p=M_1^p. The three-state upper-triangular entries give an exact sign polynomial with a single root in (0,1), and direct entry inequalities prove the iff cutoff for every p. verify.py checked the exact identities from the same package (symbolic rational algebra); infinite p follows from proof, not enumeration.

limitations: The 3-state sharp threshold applies to a particular equal-rate pure-birth split; p is finite positive integer and arithmetic exact. Scientific validity has only a self-review, not independent audit.

value.rationale: Negative linear weights in extrapolated positivity-preserving substeps motivate an exact state-size safety diagnosis. The theorem characterizes every 2-state row Markov splitting, not one example, and proves a structurally non-obvious collapse of delayed aggregation to iterated extrapolation. In the smallest possible counterexample, an exact log-algebraic positivity frontier remains invariant under arbitrary aggregation delay, a concrete constraint for latency-reduced integrators. The exact threshold is intrinsic to an equal-rate 3-state two-edge Markov system, not an arbitrary finite invariant.
